title: Research how sleep affects student learning
description: Prepare a short, source-backed research brief on sleep quality and learning outcomes for college students.
topic: Sleep and learning outcomes in college students
brief: Research how sleep duration and quality may affect memory, attention, and academic performance in college students. Compare at least three credible sources, include one useful statistic, and finish with a short list of practical takeaways.

title: Explore ways campuses can reduce food waste
description: Find practical approaches universities can use to reduce food waste in dining halls.
topic: Reducing food waste in university dining
brief: Look into common causes of food waste in campus dining halls and compare at least three reduction strategies. Use reputable sources, describe one campus example, and explain which strategy seems easiest for a student union to try.

title: Compare AI study tools for university students
description: Research how students use AI study tools and what benefits or concerns come with them.
brief: Compare at least three AI-assisted study tools or use cases. Research potential benefits, accuracy or privacy concerns, and responsible-use guidance from credible sources. Include a concise comparison table in your report.

title: Investigate public transport for students
description: Look into how public transport access and fares affect students getting to campus.
brief: Research the costs and availability of public transport for students in a city or region you choose. Compare at least two fare-support approaches and cite reliable transport-agency or research sources. State your chosen location in the report.

title: Study social media and student focus
description: Summarize current evidence on social media use, attention, and study habits.
topic: Social media use and study focus
brief: Review at least three credible sources about social media use and student attention or study habits. Distinguish correlation from causation, note any limitations in the evidence, and end with balanced study-habit suggestions.

title: Assess solar power for a university campus
description: Research the benefits and practical challenges of adding solar power to campus buildings.
brief: Research the likely benefits, costs, and practical challenges of installing solar panels on university buildings. Find one real campus example and use credible sources for your claims. End with a short recommendation and explain its trade-offs.

title: Research budgeting tips for first-year students
description: Compare practical ways new university students can plan spending and manage limited income.
topic: Budgeting strategies for first-year university students
brief: Find advice from at least three credible student-finance or education sources. Compare budgeting methods, common expense categories, and realistic saving approaches. Include a sample monthly student budget and cite your sources.

title: Find ways to conserve water on campus
description: Explore effective water-saving measures for university buildings and student housing.
brief: Research at least three water-saving measures used by universities or public buildings. Compare expected impact, cost, and ease of implementation, using credible sources and one real-world example.

title: Review student mental-health support options
description: Map common support services universities offer and what makes them accessible.
topic: Access to mental-health support for university students
brief: Use reputable health or university sources to summarize common mental-health support options for students. Compare accessibility, privacy, and referral pathways. Keep the report informational and avoid giving medical advice.

title: Compare renewable energy options for schools
description: Compare solar, wind, and other renewable energy options that may suit educational campuses.
topic: Renewable energy choices for educational campuses
brief: Compare at least three renewable energy options for a school or university. Explain likely costs, site needs, maintenance, and environmental impact. Use credible sources and identify which option suits one chosen campus context.

title: Investigate what helps students learn online
description: Summarize research on engagement, access, and outcomes in online university courses.
topic: Effective online learning in higher education
brief: Compare evidence on student engagement and learning in online courses. Cover at least three factors such as feedback, course structure, internet access, or peer connection. Cite credible education research and note evidence limitations.

title: Explore the benefits of university community gardens
description: Research how campus gardens can support learning, wellbeing, and local food access.
brief: Find real university garden examples and research possible educational, wellbeing, and food-system benefits. Compare practical challenges such as land, water, maintenance, and participation. Include at least three cited sources.

title: Assess options for reducing single-use plastics
description: Look at practical alternatives to single-use plastic in campus cafés and events.
brief: Compare reusable, recyclable, and compostable options for campus food service. Research actual disposal infrastructure and life-cycle trade-offs, then make a practical recommendation supported by sources.

title: Create a student guide to safer online accounts
description: Research common account-security risks and evidence-based protections for students.
brief: Use reputable cybersecurity guidance to explain phishing, password reuse, multi-factor authentication, and device updates. Write practical steps for a student audience and cite authoritative sources.

title: Research inclusive and accessible campus design
description: Explore how universal design can make learning spaces easier for more students to use.
topic: Inclusive design in higher education spaces
brief: Research universal-design principles for classrooms and campus facilities. Compare at least three design interventions, refer to credible accessibility guidance, and explain how to involve students in evaluating changes.

title: Explore challenges facing commuter students
description: Research how commuting affects student time, participation, and access to campus services.
brief: Review credible research on commuter students’ experiences. Explore travel time, campus schedules, cost, and belonging, then summarize practical university supports with cited evidence.

title: Research how food labels guide student choices
description: Look at nutrition, allergen, and sustainability information in campus food settings.
brief: Research how nutrition, allergen, and sustainability labels influence food choices. Use public-health or academic sources, compare examples, and recommend clear, accessible information for a campus café.

title: Compare e-bikes and other student commute options
description: Review the costs, safety, and environmental impacts of short-distance campus travel.
brief: Compare walking, cycling, e-bikes, and public transport for a short student commute. Consider affordability, safety, accessibility, and emissions using credible sources. State assumptions and cite evidence.

title: Find what makes a good university study space
description: Research how noise, lighting, seating, and access affect student study environments.
brief: Research design factors that influence focus and comfort in study spaces. Compare quiet areas, collaborative zones, lighting, seating, and opening hours using at least three credible sources and real campus examples.

title: Explain digital privacy basics for university students
description: Summarize useful steps students can take to protect personal information online.
brief: Use guidance from privacy regulators or recognized security organizations to explain app permissions, data sharing, public Wi-Fi, and account settings. Make a concise student-friendly checklist with citations.

title: Explore how libraries support student success
description: Research library services beyond books, including digital access and study support.
topic: University library services and student outcomes
brief: Research how academic libraries support learning through resources, digital access, research skills, and inclusive spaces. Use at least three credible sources and include an example of a useful service.

title: Review climate education in higher education
description: Explore ways universities include climate literacy across different subjects.
brief: Research approaches to climate education across disciplines. Compare course integration, campus projects, and community partnerships, using educational sources and examples from universities.

title: Research food security among university students
description: Summarize evidence on student food insecurity and evaluate campus support approaches.
topic: Food security and support for university students
brief: Use credible research to describe factors associated with student food insecurity. Compare campus food pantries, meal support, and policy approaches, while treating the subject respectfully and citing evidence.

title: Compare assistive technologies for university study
description: Explore digital tools that can improve access to course material for disabled students.
brief: Compare several assistive technologies or accessibility features used in higher education. Explain the learning barriers they may address, note limitations, and use reputable accessibility and education sources.
